title: MANEESH SEMWAL EXECUTIVE ENGINEER versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND
judges: ["Hon'ble Mr. Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Siddhartha Sah"]

paras.text:
UKHC010158482026
2026:UHC:8093-DB
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Bench No. 587 of 2026
09 September, 2026
Maneesh Semwal, Executive Engineer and another
 --Petitioners
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others --Respondents
Present:-
Mr. D.S. Patni, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr.
Dharmendra Barthwal and Mr. Tribhuwan Singh Phartiyal,
learned counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. Rajeev Bisht, learned DAG along with Mr. Ranjan Ghildiyal,
learned Standing Counsel for the State/respondent nos.1 and
2.
Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi and Ms. Neeti Rana, learned counsel for
respondent nos.3 and 4.
Mr. Anil Bisht, learned counsel for respondent no.9.
Coram:Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
 Hon'ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J. (Oral)
Petitioners as well as respondent nos. 5 to 11 are
serving as Executive Engineer. The next promotional post
available to Executive Engineer is that of Superintending
Engineer. Rule 6(5) of the Uttarakhand Jal Sansthan
Engineering Service Rules, 2011 provides for qualifying
service, which reads as under:-
"6-(5) Superintendent Engineer - By promotion
on the basis of seniority subject to rejection from
amongst the substantively appointed Assistant
Engineers. Executive Engineers, who have
completed 15 years service (including atleast 6

UKHC010158482026
2026:UHC:8093-DB
2
years service as Executive Engineer) on the first
day of the year of recruitment."
2. There were 11 vacancies available on the post of
Superintendent Engineer which were to be filled by
promotion alone. State Government, by invoking its power
under Rule 4 of the Uttarakhand Government Servants
Relaxation in Qualifying Service for Promotion Rules, 2025,
granted relaxation to respondent nos. 5 to 11. Petitioners
have challenged the said order dated 24.07.2026, whereby
relaxation was granted. Impugned order is enclosed as
Annexure-1 to the writ petition. Perusal of the same reveals
that benefit of relaxation would be available to respondent
nos. 5 to 11, only if all persons senior to them have been
promoted, and the private respondents will not be entitled to
any career progression which results in their holding a
position superior to their seniors.
3. Learned counsel for the parties are unanimous on
the point that the private respondents are en-bloc senior to
petitioners. Petitioners stand at serial nos. 26 and 36,
respectively, in the seniority list of Assistant Engineer, while
the private respondents stand at serial nos. 6, 8, 10, 12, 14,
22 and 24 in the seniority list. Thus, it is nobody's case that
relaxation in qualifying service given to private respondents

UKHC010158482026
2026:UHC:8093-DB
3
may result in their holding a position superior to their
seniors.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that
there were 11 vacancies on the post of Superintending
Engineer and there were 14 persons serving as Executive
Engineer, who fulfilled the eligibility conditions necessary for
promotion; therefore, there was no need to expand the zone
of consideration by granting relaxation in qualifying service.
5. Learned counsel for the respondents, however,
submit that as per Rule 19(2) of applicable service rules,
where promotion is to be made on the criteria of seniority
subject to rejection of unfit, for five or more vacancies,
eligibility list should consist of one and half times the
number of vacancies, subject to a minimum of 10. Thus,
learned counsels for respondents submit that even if the
contention raised on behalf of petitioners is taken at its face
value that there were 14 eligible Executive Engineers, then
also it does not meet the requirement of Rule 19(2), as the
eligibility list should consist of not less than 17 candidates
for 11 vacancies. Learned counsels further submit that
petitioners as well as respondent nos. 5 to 11 participated in
the same selection, however, respondent nos. 5 to 11, even
though had scored more marks, but were slightly late in

UKHC010158482026
2026:UHC:8093-DB
4
joining duties; therefore, the service rendered by them fell
short of what was required, and seniority dispute between
the parties is separately pending in Writ Petition No. 456 of
2025 (SB) before the Coordinate Bench.
6. Thus, it is contended that since the private
respondents were senior, but were not able to meet the
condition of Rule 6(5) due to fortuitous circumstances,
therefore, relaxation in qualifying service was given to them
to ensure that they are not deprived of their rightful claim to
promotion. It is further contended that if relaxation was not
given to private respondents, then eligibility list would not be
complete, as a minimum of 17 candidates would be needed
in the eligibility list against 11 vacancies on the post of
Superintending Engineer.
7. Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi, learned counsel appearing
for respondent nos. 3 and 4, points out that DPC meeting
was held on 31.08.2026 and recommendation was made for
promotion against the available vacancies. Thus, he submits
that the relief as claimed by petitioners does not survive once
the Departmental Promotion Committee met and considered
the eligible persons, including those who were given
relaxation in qualifying service.

UKHC010158482026
2026:UHC:8093-DB
5
8. This Court do not find any reason to interfere in
the matter. Admittedly, petitioners are junior to the persons
who were given relaxation in qualifying service. As per Rule
19(2), the eligibility list should contain names one and half
times the number of existing vacancies. Criteria for
promotion is seniority subject to rejection of unfit.
Petitioners concede that there were only 14 Executive
Engineers who possessed all conditions of eligibility for
promotion to the post of Superintending Engineer. As per
Rule 19 of the applicable rules, against 11 vacancies, the
eligibility list should contain 17 names. Thus, the shortfall of
three candidates was required to be made good by granting
relaxation in qualifying service.
9. Since respondent Nos. 5 to 11 are all placed above
petitioners in the final seniority list, the State Government,
in its wisdom, decided to grant relaxation to all of them with
the condition that, on the strength of such relaxation, private
respondents will not hold a position superior to their seniors.
Granting relaxation to only three persons and not granting
relaxation to other similarly situated persons, would have
caused heartburn to those who were not granted such
benefit; therefore, the State Government, in its wisdom,
decided to grant relaxation to all senior persons. Rule 4 of
the Relaxation Rules, 2025, enables the State Government to

UKHC010158482026
2026:UHC:8093-DB
6
grant relaxation in qualifying service whenever required
number of persons are not available in the field of eligibility,
and it does not impose any restriction regarding the
maximum number of persons to whom such benefit can be
granted. Thus, the decision taken by the State Government,
which was communicated by the impugned order dated
24.07.2026, cannot be said to be arbitrary or illegal.
10. Thus, there is hardly any scope for interference in
the matter. Accordingly, present writ petition fails and is
dismissed.
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
